title: Speculative Decoding
summary: Use a cheap proposal mechanism and target-model verification to reduce decoding latency only where acceptance and workload conditions justify the overhead.
overview: Speculative decoding accelerates autoregressive generation by proposing several tokens with a cheaper draft mechanism and verifying them with the target model. Accepted proposals let the system advance more than one token per target verification cycle. Implementations may use a separate draft model, auxiliary prediction heads, or non-model proposals such as matching prompt patterns.

Correct speculative sampling algorithms preserve the target distribution under their stated assumptions; arbitrary acceptance shortcuts do not. Speedup is workload-dependent. Draft cost, acceptance rate, verification efficiency, batch size, and memory pressure determine whether speculation helps. It can be attractive for some memory-bound, moderate-load workloads and unhelpful when the serving system is already compute-saturated.

production.poc: A prototype measures draft acceptance and end-to-end latency against the same target model without speculation.
production.production: Production evaluates output equivalence requirements, draft compatibility, resource overhead, and fallback to ordinary decoding.
production.scale: At scale, enable speculation selectively by workload and load state, and re-benchmark after engine, model, hardware, or batching changes.

components.name: Draft proposer
components.role: Generates a bounded sequence of candidate next tokens cheaply.

components.name: Target verifier
components.role: Evaluates proposals using the authoritative target model.

components.name: Acceptance sampler
components.role: Applies the correct accept or reject procedure for the decoding configuration.

components.name: Cache coordinator
components.role: Maintains consistent target and draft sequence state after accepted and rejected tokens.

components.name: Adaptive controller
components.role: Chooses proposal length or disables speculation using observed benefit.

flow.title: Assess workload suitability
flow.description: Check current batch pressure, target latency, and available memory for the proposal mechanism.

flow.title: Produce draft tokens
flow.description: Generate a short candidate continuation under the supported configuration.

flow.title: Verify in target model
flow.description: Score the proposed sequence with the authoritative model in a batched verification step.

flow.title: Accept or correct
flow.description: Advance through accepted tokens and use the algorithm’s correction rule at rejection.

flow.title: Reconcile sequence state
flow.description: Discard invalid speculative state and retain caches for the accepted prefix.

flow.title: Adapt using measurements
flow.description: Track accepted tokens per verification cycle and compare actual latency with the non-speculative baseline.

diagrams.caption: Verification remains authoritative, and rejected speculative state must not leak into the accepted sequence.

useCase.title: Reducing latency in repetitive configuration answers
useCase.situation: A technical assistant produces structured configuration guidance with recurring syntax and terminology.
useCase.problem: Users wait on token-by-token decoding even though many continuations are predictable.
useCase.requirement: Reduce response latency without changing the accepted target-model behavior.
useCase.architecture: The serving engine uses a compatible draft mechanism and tracks acceptance separately for configuration and exploratory questions.
runtime: A configuration answer accepts several proposed tokens per verification cycle.
An open-ended diagnostic question with poor acceptance falls back to standard decoding.
useCase.failure: During a traffic surge, speculation is disabled if draft overhead worsens queueing and total latency.
useCase.impact: Measure time to completion, inter-token latency, throughput, and memory under realistic concurrency; isolated single-request speedups do not establish fleet benefit.

tradeoffs.cost: Waste more draft work when acceptance is low.
Requires stable measurements and control thresholds.

failures.detection: Draft work rises without enough accepted tokens.
failures.recovery: Reduce proposal length or disable speculation for that task.

failures.detection: Outputs or engine checks reveal inconsistent sequence state.
failures.recovery: Use validated engine implementations and revert to ordinary decoding.

mistakes.fix: Benchmark the actual load and output distribution.

mistakes.mistake: Assuming any verification rule preserves quality
mistakes.fix: Use the supported correct sampling algorithm.
Include draft and cache overhead in capacity planning.

whenToUse: Use when measured draft acceptance is high.
Use for latency-sensitive workloads with suitable capacity.
Use with a supported verified engine implementation.
whenNotToUse: Avoid when speculation worsens saturated throughput.
Do not use incompatible draft and target configurations.
Avoid enabling it solely from a microbenchmark.
checklist: Include draft memory and compute cost.
